searchText: **n0ble** > things make a lot more sense when you're fresh Monday morning than they do late Friday afternoon. Indeed 😆 I am wondering if any team has started to look into incremental and/or compressed storage for beacon state? **svantemand** Hey @CarlBeek, I just noticed the notes on BLS here: https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/releases/tag/v0.9.1 "Warning: Bug exists in BLS hash to G2 in the current spec. The hash and increment approach will be deprecated after standardization so the bug is to be untouched for now_ Significant changes still expected as we standardize BLS12-381 across blockchains" Is this new info or are we still on track to finalize spec after IETF meeting? **CarlBeek** That note has been there a long time. It has nothing to do with the standardisation efforts, but the way hashing was implemented in the spec a long time ago. It was decided to leave it like that untill the standardiastion efforts have enshrined the new hash-to-curve to prevent spec chrun. The intention is to update the specs as soon as the standard is agreed upon.

excerpts.author: eth2_bridge_bot
excerpts.content:
**svantemand**
Hey @CarlBeek, I just noticed the notes on BLS here:
https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/releases/tag/v0.9.1

"Warning: Bug exists in BLS hash to G2 in the current spec. The hash and increment approach will be deprecated after standardization so the bug is to be untouched for now_

Significant changes still expected as we standardize BLS12-381 across blockchains"

Is this new info or are we still on track to finalize spec after IETF meeting?

excerpts.author: eth2_bridge_bot
excerpts.content:
**CarlBeek**
That note has been there a long time. It has nothing to do with the standardisation efforts, but the way hashing was implemented in the spec a long time ago. It was decided to leave it like that untill the standardiastion efforts have enshrined the new hash-to-curve to prevent spec chrun. The intention is to update the specs as soon as the standard is agreed upon.
